title: Ransomware outage of production systems
risk_statement: If a threat actor gains a foothold via phishing or exposed remote access and deploys ransomware, then production servers and file shares may be encrypted, resulting in a multi-day outage of order processing, recovery costs, and extortion over exfiltrated data.
assets_affected: ERP, file servers, virtualization cluster, backup infrastructure
existing_controls: Email filtering with attachment detonation; EDR on all endpoints and servers; MFA on VPN and email; network segmentation between user and server VLANs; immutable offline backups with quarterly restore tests
control_refs: AC-POL-01; ISO 27001 A.8.7 / A.8.13; CIS v8 Controls 10-11; NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS / RC.RP
treatment_plan: Deploy phishing-resistant MFA to remaining 30% of workforce; complete PAM rollout for domain admin accounts; run annual ransomware tabletop with executive participation
notes: Cyber insurance policy CY-2026-114 covers incident response and business interruption; last tabletop 2026-02-12

title: Breach of employee PII at payroll SaaS provider
risk_statement: If the payroll SaaS provider suffers a breach of its multi-tenant platform, then employee PII including bank details for 1,200 staff may be exposed, resulting in regulatory notification obligations, credit-monitoring costs, and loss of employee trust.
assets_affected: Employee PII (names, addresses, national IDs, bank details) processed by payroll provider
existing_controls: Vendor tiered as critical with annual reassessment; SOC 2 Type II report reviewed annually; DPA requires provider breach notification within 48 hours; SSO with MFA enforced for admin console; data minimization - records older than 7 years purged
treatment_plan: Add contractual audit right at 2026-11 renewal; obtain provider penetration test summary; enable SCIM deprovisioning to remove dormant admin accounts
notes: A provider breach would trigger a GDPR Art. 33 assessment for EU staff and US state breach-law analysis for US staff

title: Exploitation of unpatched internet-facing VPN appliance
risk_statement: If the internet-facing VPN appliance remains unpatched against known exploited vulnerabilities, then an attacker may gain remote access to the internal network, resulting in credential theft, lateral movement, and potential full domain compromise.
assets_affected: VPN appliance, Active Directory, all internally reachable systems
existing_controls: Monthly external vulnerability scans; 14-day patch SLA for critical internet-facing CVEs; IPS signatures at perimeter; appliance admin interface restricted to management VLAN
control_refs: VULN-STD-01; CIS v8 Control 7; ISO 27001 A.8.8
treatment_plan: Enroll appliance in emergency out-of-band patching for known-exploited vulnerabilities; evaluate ZTNA replacement by Q1 2027; route exploit-attempt alerts from perimeter logs to SOC
notes: EXC-2025-014 defers firmware upgrade 30 days pending vendor fix for HA cluster bug; expires 2026-08-10
